464-10-A15: We bought the best AI system on the market. Staff got a one-hour webinar.
Me? I have people for that.
464-10-A18: The machine assigns the raids. It rates you in secret. The lowest goes out of the gate every month. Appeal? To whom?
464-10-A20: (checking each against the patrols he knows) B crosses the east patrol at nine. A, then. My call.
464-10-A21: (daily) Captain, here's the news — oh, and thanks for yesterday.
(a day's ride away, a week later) Did the captain say anything about us?
464-10-A23: (nailing a single page to the gate) What the machine is for. What it must never do. Who checks it before the gate opens. Who answers when it's wrong — me.
464-10-A25: All our gold on the seeing-machine. Think of it!
Half the gold on the machine — and the rest teaching every guard to read it, for a month.
464-10-A26: The machine is installed! The defence is complete!
464-10-A28: (to the village) It's not about what the machine does. It tells us when the east road is empty — so the children can walk to school.
464-10-A29: (every morning, at the gate, in front of the guards) Right. Let's see what the machine says today.
464-10-A30: Lussier and Achua, chapter 12. The kind of organisation a digital transformation forces a leader to build. Not a control-based one — a…?
464-10-A31: We only ever hear from him when something goes wrong. The near ones talk to him every day.
(to Rami) There's a rhythm for this. The chapter has it.
464-10-A32: How do I judge the far scouts? Hours on watch? Signals sent?
Or — did the pass stay safe?
464-10-A33: The far scouts: slower to be promoted, never given the interesting missions. Not because you decided — because you can't see them.
That's… the thing from the diversity chapter, isn't it?
464-10-A34: Scout Dana: 4 signals per hour. Scout Omar: 11.
Is 'signals per hour' something the valley would notice — or just something the device can count?
464-10-A35: (the device says 'Dana: disengaged') If I act on this and I'm wrong — who pays? And could I explain it to her, face to face?
464-10-A36: (editing, then signing it) Draft's yours. The choice is mine — and so is the blame.
464-10-A37: From today the machine's rules are written on the gate. And if it's wrong about you — go to old Salim. He can change it.
464-10-A38: (a notice) 'This message was written by the seeing-machine.' (another) 'This one was written by me.'
464-10-A39: A national AI strategy. A charter with principles. Chief AI Officers in government. Why does the chapter call the UAE 'an unusually good classroom' for this?
464-10-A40: (before anything has gone wrong) Crisis team: Noor, Salim, me. Risk list: on the wall. The message we'll give the village if the machine fails: already written.
464-02-A01: In the Mirror Cave each rescuer sees their own true nature.
464-02-A14: Noor, you can find the path. I trust you.
…Then I will find it. Follow me.
464-02-A28: Take the gold, captain. Forget the girl. Nobody will ever know.
Would I want to be the one left behind in that tower?
464-03-A01: Table six, layout B. Order in at 12:04 — I want it out by 12:16. No, I don't need your ideas, I need your hands.
Yes, boss. (to a waiter) That's the third cook who quit this month.
The food is always on time. The staff never stay.
464-03-A02: Don't worry about the deadline, Hamad — your health comes first. We'll explain it to the client somehow.
Thanks… that's the third one we've missed this quarter, though.
Let's not talk about that now. Cake in the kitchen!
464-03-A03: Morning. Today: the east wall to the second floor, zero incidents. Can we do it?
With the second crane, yes. We'll need it by ten.
You'll have it. I'll check at noon — and I'm buying lunch.
464-03-A04: Ask head office. I just sign the timesheets.
Target this week is… the usual. You're doing… fine. Let's keep the peace.
464-03-A09: Rashid, the salary came on time — thanks. But Zoom Eats pays 400 more for the same shifts.
I know, Ali. I can't change the salary scale this month.
Then at least don't lose us over the small things.
464-03-A10: Forty-five a day? I did 38 and my legs were gone. Only Omar's group hits it.
And the bonus from September? Still not paid.
464-03-A11: Why does Omar always get Al Majaz? Short roads, big tips.
He's fast because he gets Al Majaz. The rest of us get the desert.
464-03-A12: Eleven on-time deliveries today and the only message is about the twelfth.
So just don't be late. Don't be anything else either.
464-03-A13: Same forty streets, every day, for three years. Who became dispatcher last time?
Nobody. Head office hires from outside.
Then this is a job, not a future.
464-03-A16: Ali — forty-five, all on time, in the rain. That is exactly why our rating stays above 4.8.
Same again tomorrow? I'll be watching for it.
464-03-A19: Good job on the slides, Maha.
464-03-A21: The fortress by dawn. Forty kilometres, over the pass, in the dark.
Captain, no one can do that. Not even me.
464-03-A22: Dana, your tracking today was brilliant.
C-can we talk about it after I find a blanket, captain?
464-03-A23: If we cross at the old mill, the gang won't see us.
Nobody answers. Omar keeps sharpening his knife; Rami studies the map.
464-03-A24: Omar — anchor rope, left tree. Noor — you cross second. Dana — count to ten before you follow. I check every knot.
464-03-A25: I carried the tent, the ropes and the water. She carried a scarf. Same bread, same meat.
464-03-A29: Three ways across the marsh. You've all walked it before — which one?
The next morning, they cross without being told.
464-03-A33: Nobody noticed I found the water.
(that evening, to all) Omar found the water. Without him we'd be drinking mud.
464-04-A01: Everyone out through door B, now. Rashid, kill the main valve. Nobody argues, nobody votes.
464-04-A02: Last time they changed the booking system, nobody asked us — and we spent a year working around it.
I'm not an IT person. You know where the queues really come from.
Then let us design it with you. We'll own it if we build it.
464-04-A03: Last time I wrote production code, the framework you're discussing didn't exist.
We've benchmarked three options. We can decide by Friday if you give us the constraints.
Budget, security review, and it must run on our cloud. Within that — it's yours.
464-04-A04: Sir… the customer says the invoice is wrong and he's shouting. I've never seen this screen.
Breathe. Click 'Billing', then 'Dispute'. Read him the reference number. I'll stand right here.
464-04-A05: We sold it. The warehouse couldn't ship it. And now our numbers say we failed.
Your numbers say the warehouse failed — I've told the board that in writing. This quarter, I've got your back.
464-04-A07: Good morning, everyone. I know the last head left suddenly, and I know he decided everything alone.
We heard the new head will be different. We've heard that before.
Then judge me by the next six weeks, not by my speech.
464-04-A10: Go-live is in six weeks. Every user needs four hours of training.
Then I set the timetable: doctors Tuesday, nurses Wednesday, reception Thursday. I'll ask each of you one thing — which day is impossible for you.
464-04-A11: Waiting time has doubled. I have three theories and I suspect all three are wrong.
The doctors say reception; reception says the lab; the lab says the doctors.
Then Thursday, all of you, one room, one whiteboard. We find it together — and I decide only when we've looked.
464-04-A12: Dr Lina, Dr Yousef — protocol review with me every morning for a month, and I expect you to lead a case by week four.
Every morning. Dr Hassan, your clinics are yours — I'll only ask for the monthly numbers.
464-04-A15: I always let the team decide. I just set the limits.
You set the limits, the plan, the slides and the colour scheme.
464-04-A18: Two paths. One is shorter; one is safer. If I pick and you don't believe in it, we'll turn back halfway.
The left pass floods after rain. I grew up here.
Then tell me everything, all of you — and we pick one we'll all walk.
464-04-A19: We have drilled for the gang for years. Tell us the time; we know the rest.
Then I'll get you the horses and keep the gang off your flank.
464-04-A21: Omar — the north face. Nobody on this mountain can do it faster than you. Top by noon?
464-04-A27: Two rules: no fires, back by dusk. Within that, the route is yours.
All of it. I'll be here.
464-05-A01: Forty-one alarm failures in six months. Nine delayed responses. Here is the chart, and here is what each one cost.
…Send me the quote for the monitors.
464-05-A02: Before Thursday — have you both read the proposal? If you agree with it, I'd like the director to hear it from you too.
I agree with sections one and three. I'll say so. Section two, you're on your own.
464-05-A03: Khalid, that's the third time this month. The policy says I have to issue a written warning now — I'm not choosing it, the rule is.
464-05-A04: You hated the plan. Fine — help me fix it. Which part would you change first?
The rollout order. Give me a week.
A week later, Faris presents the plan to the board himself.
464-05-A05: Finish the report tonight or your leave is cancelled.
(quietly) Then I'll finish the report. And I'll remember this.
The report arrives at midnight. The technician's loyalty does not.
464-05-A06: I'm not asking for a job — just twenty minutes on how you moved into strategy. And if you can think of two people I should talk to…
Twenty minutes I have. And yes — two names. Write this down.
464-05-A08: One pilot week. The new template takes the field teams 2.3 hours a day. The old one took one.
Everyone in the field knows it. Nobody will say it to your manager — he designed it.
I have the numbers. I just don't have the chair.
464-05-A10: I ran a pilot week on the template, but I'm not sure one week is representative. Could you help me check how I should test it?
Three. Here are the hours. If it holds up across six, the director's data will come late.
464-05-A13: Could we look at the workload figures together — just the three pilot teams?
If they hold, I'd like to trial the simpler version for two weeks. If not — someone other than me should review the data.
464-05-A16: Understood — it's your call. Would you mind if I keep tracking the field hours for a month and bring you the figures either way?
464-05-A17: Hi. I'm a student. I need a job. Do you have one?
464-05-A19: I'm not climbing that ridge. Not for you, not for anyone.
I am the captain of this party. You will march.
464-05-A20: You know ridges better than I do. If the ridge is wrong, show me a better way.
…There's a goat path on the north side. I'll take you up it myself.
464-05-A21: Omar. Layla taught your sister to read. Think of that when you look at the fortress.
(silent, then stands) Give me the rope.
464-05-A22: Four days' food, or you swim.
Two days' food, tonight — or we take the old bridge at dawn and you earn nothing.
464-05-A29: As chief, I order the north field cleared by Friday.
(aside) A month ago they'd have told you the north field floods on Thursday.
464-05-A32: I don't do politics. My route is better. That's enough.
The council chooses the miller's route. The miller talked to every elder the night before.
Your route was better. His was supported.
464-06-A01: She told us this hospital could be the best in the region — and somehow we started believing it.
Thursday, two o'clock, my office. Bring the case you're least sure about. We'll go through it together.
464-06-A02: Hit the number, get the bonus. Miss it, we talk. Otherwise, I'm not here.
He's fair. He's clear. Nobody's ever been excited.
464-06-A03: The app idea? Mine. The pricing? Mine. The deputy who disagreed? Gone — like the two before him.
What happens if he's ever not here?
464-06-A04: The timetable is yours to design. The award is yours too — I only signed the form.
She is the person who made me a better teacher.
464-06-A05: Today we begin the reform that will change this ministry forever!
Two years later. The speeches are famous. The ministry's structure, rewards and procedures are exactly as before.
Beautiful speech. Nothing on my desk changed.
464-06-A08: When the bank called in the loan, everyone said we were finished. He walked in and said 'we're not'. And we believed him.
…I'm not sure. But we believed him.
464-06-A09: I was wrong about the Oman launch. Say it with me — Khalid was wrong. Now — who has a better plan?
I do. And since you gave me the division, I'll run it.
464-06-A14: What was the organisation like when you took over — and what did you have to convince people of?
That we were dying slowly. Nobody believed it because the numbers still looked fine.
464-06-A15: What is this company trying to become?
The first in the Gulf to run every warehouse without paper. Why — did he say the same?
464-06-A18: The night the gang came, everyone ran. He didn't. He stood in the square and said 'we go and get her back'.
And we followed. We'd have followed him anywhere that night.
464-06-A19: Who questioned me? Nobody. Good. Nobody questions me.
(whispering) If he falls, we all fall.
464-06-A21: We are not four people chasing a gang. We are the reason this valley will sleep safely again.
…When you put it like that, I can walk another ten miles.
464-06-A26: Rami? He's a good man. He runs the mill now.
A year ago you called him the valley's saviour.
A year ago we needed one.
464-07-A01: Step 14 says the form must be stamped in blue. It has been stamped in blue since 2009.
By next year 80% of this will be online. There will be no stamp.
…Then what colour will the online stamp be?
464-07-A02: Product two died. Pizza's on me — tell me the three things we learned.
We learned the corridor is where we decide things.
Correct. Next decision, corridor, five minutes.
464-07-A03: Forty years I have worked here. We decide everything together, like a family.
The new store across the road is 20% cheaper. We have been discussing a response for six weeks.
Then let us discuss it again on Thursday, after Fatima's birthday.
464-07-A04: So we all agree on the new schedule?
No — it's wrong in three places.
Tom disagrees as usual. The engineers agree. Carried.
(to himself) It's wrong in five places.
464-07-A05: Our values are on every wall: integrity first.
And Ziad, with two mis-selling complaints, was promoted last month.
So the wall says one thing and the promotion says another.
464-07-A06: We are a family here. Read the code — it's on the wall.
And the depot supervisor who altered the delivery log?
He delivers. Twenty years. Fix it quietly.
464-07-A09: The young South Asian drivers are leaving. Two this month.
That is just how it is here.
Not any more. Formal investigation, same standard as for anyone — and the outcome principle goes on the same wall as the code.
464-07-A12: Sir, with respect — the law prohibits what the review found, and the culture is already paying: the drivers are leaving.
We may lose the fastest depot for a quarter. Keep this, and we lose every depot that watches what we do next.
464-07-A15: What story do new joiners hear in their first week?
The one about the founder driving a delivery himself at midnight. Everyone hears it.
So the value is… nobody is above the work.
464-07-A18: Does anyone think the plan is wrong?
Silence. Forty villagers look at the ground.
(later, quietly) Three of them think it's wrong. They told me behind the well.
464-07-A19: In this village, everyone is treated the same.
Then why does your cousin ride the grey horse again?
464-07-A21: I am afraid. I will tell you what I know and what I don't. And I will not take the elders' road — not because I am brave, but because it is wrong.
You admit fear and still disobey us?
464-07-A23: The gate guard took gold from the gang. I saw it.
And you — you bring shame on the village by saying it. Leave the hall.
So the next person who sees something will say nothing.
464-07-A30: (shouting) Who lost the map?! …That's just who I am, Noor. I don't pretend.
Authentic is fine. Unchanged is a choice.
464-08-A01: Our statement: 'We will be the most trusted healthcare provider in the Northern Emirates.'
Ambitious, memorable, about the future. But it doesn't tell me what to do on Monday.
Monday comes from the objectives. This is where we're going.
464-08-A03: This year's objective: improve customer service.
Improve it to what? By when? Measured how?
464-08-A04: Twenty years. I know every form by its colour. Now a screen?
The strategy says two years, all digital.
Then in two years I'll be the slowest person in the office.
464-08-A05: The new app picks my route. Fewer parcels per hour — fewer dirhams.
Same-day delivery is what the competitor launched. We have to.
Then show me how I don't lose money. Otherwise I'll keep my own route.
464-08-A06: The new assessment system starts this term. Professor Nabil, Professor Reem — you have not uploaded a rubric.
Our exams have worked for twenty years.
Then help me design the new system so it keeps what worked in yours. Nobody knows assessment here better than you two.
464-08-A07: Six months since the town hall. Adoption is 35%. What was the objective?
There wasn't one with a number. There was a video about 'the future'.
464-08-A09: I keep a paper copy. Twenty-two years, never lost a pallet.
And I scan it, and then it exists twice, and nobody knows which is right.
(on the phone) Did anyone remember Fujairah exists?
464-08-A11: Jaber, nobody knows this warehouse like you. I want you to run the training for the new system.
Me? I don't even like the system.
That's why you're the right trainer. Tell the vendor what's wrong with it first.
464-08-A16: 'To be a global leader in a knowledge-based future.' Would you recognise your job in that?
My job is renewing licences. So… no.
464-08-A19: The tunnel roof gives way. Dust. Silence. The map in Rami's hand now leads into rock.
We can dig through. Three days.
Look at it, Omar. There is no 'through'. We let the old plan go — tonight.
464-08-A20: I'm not climbing. I'll go round the long way.
(quietly, to Rami) She's never climbed. She doesn't want Omar to see her slow.
Omar — rope up with Dana. First pitch together. When she tops it, we all see it.
464-08-A22: Picture it: a valley where every child walks to school without fear.
No. It's why we'll make one.
464-09-A01: I thought it was me. I already called him.
Why have two of you called me and neither knows what the other said?
464-09-A02: (in front of the whole ward) You are ALWAYS late with the charts.
Next week, the charts are late again. Nothing was specified, nothing was asked, nothing was owned.
464-09-A03: The load path has to go through the core.
It can't — the core is already at capacity.
Work it out between you. I've got a call.
A week later, they communicate only through the shared drive.
464-09-A05: Before I decide — Sara, Yousef, what do you two think?
(to a colleague) He's asked them first for a year. Why would we bother?
464-09-A06: Right — ninety minutes, five topics. Any decisions?
Good idea. Same time next week.
464-09-A07: 9 p.m. again. Appraisals done — now the weekly reports.
I could do the reports. I've watched you do them for two years.
…The reports, yes. The appraisals stay with me.
464-09-A08: So we assume the client's data is quarterly. Moving on.
Great energy, everyone! Same grade for all, as always.
The quarterly assumption costs the team a week.
464-09-A10: Khalid — you've missed the last three meetings. I need you at every one and owning the market section. What would it take for you to commit to that?
…If I actually had a section, I'd come. Give me the market section.
Done. I'll check in on Thursday.
464-09-A12: When the slides arrive the night before, I rehearse at 1 a.m., and I feel the deadline isn't shared.
…That's fair. New norm: slides 48 hours before. Agreed?
464-09-A14: When did you last tell the boss something she didn't want to hear?
Never. Ask Rashid — well, you can't, he's in another department now.
464-09-A17: (across the river) Dana! Do the thing we discussed!
Which thing?! The rope or the signal?!
Dana lights the signal. Rami meant the rope.
464-09-A18: Omar — the rope went Monday, Wednesday and today. I need both hands on it until I say 'release'. Can you commit to that?
I'll watch for it at the next crossing.
464-09-A19: High ground. We need to see them coming.
Low ground. We need water and the horses are spent.
We have an hour. Find me the one place with both — and you two find it together.
464-09-A21: Noor — scout the pass. Noor — your view on the route? Noor—
(to Dana) Shall we just carry the bags, then?
464-09-A22: Dana, get us four horses by dawn.
With what? And can I promise them anything?
No gold, no promise, no horses.
464-09-A26: (reads) 'Your village was raided last night.' …He sent a note?
He should have walked the ten steps.
464-09-A28: Captain, the plan is wrong. The bridge is out.
(to the team) Noor just saved us a day. Plan changes now — and I want the next one of you who sees a mistake to say so this fast.
464-10-A01: Deactivated. 'Bottom 5%'. Bottom 5% of what? Who do I call?
This decision is final. There is no appeal.
So the boss is a formula nobody can see.
464-10-A03: Top 40: ninety percent men, three universities. The pool was fifty-five percent women.
The model weights 'university' and 'gap years' heavily. And… the rowing club.
So it learned our last ten years of hiring — and is handing them back to us.
464-10-A04: Could you tell me why I wasn't shortlisted?
Our screening tool over-weighted university and continuous employment. We found that, we are re-reviewing the pool by hand, and your application is in that review. That is the honest answer.
464-10-A06: Context: twelve agents, two senior ones threatening to resign over an AI drafting tool. Objective: an adoption plan that keeps them. Audience: me, their leader. Format: a numbered plan.
Here is a ten-point adoption plan…
Now — let's see what you got wrong about my team.
464-10-A10: If a machine writes my reply, does the customer know? And if I leave — do you tell them why?
Both questions deserve a real answer. Let me take a position, not a dodge.
464-10-A11: Twenty years of knowing exactly what to write. And now a machine drafts it.
I'm not going to tell you not to feel that. I'll tell you what changes and what doesn't — and I want you two writing the rules the machine has to follow.
464-10-A12: Section one, good. Section two, could be any company. Section three — that figure is wrong. And it has no idea Omar and Dana don't speak.
So it's a junior's first draft.
Exactly. Now I edit it like one.
464-10-A16: All my gold on the seeing-machine! Every guard watched, every door counted!
Chief — nobody knows how to read it. You spent nothing on teaching us.
The machine works, chief. We don't.
464-10-A17: The device says Dana is 'disengaged' — fewest signals all day.
Dana has been carrying the scout with the broken leg since noon.
…So the number was right and the conclusion was wrong.
464-10-A19: You built the machine. You read it. You opened the gate.
464-10-A22: The machine screams 'ATTACK!' There is no attack. The village runs.
(in the square) It was our alarm. It was wrong. Here is what failed, and here is what we do tonight so it never happens twice.
464-10-A24: The machine draws routes faster than I walk them. What's left for me?
The route it draws is a draft. Choosing it, teaching the young scouts, telling the elders no — that's you. That was always you.
464-10-A27: We've been using the seeing-glass for a month. We didn't think the elders would allow it.
Then show me what you've learned — and tomorrow you teach the rest of us.
